definitions: A coarse cloth of cotton, linen or hemp, stiffened with size or glue, used in bookbinding to cover and protect the books, in garments to keep them in the form intended, and for wrappers to cover merchandise.
A crab that has just molted; a papershell.
To stiffen with or as if with buckram.
Imposing stipulations or requirements that must be honoured.
Having the effect of counteracting diarrhea.
An item (usually rope, tape, or string) used to hold two or more things together.
The spine of a book where the pages are held together.

blocks.text: Buckram is a stiff cotton, or occasionally, linen or horse-hair cloth with a plain, usually loose, weave, produced in various weights similar to muslin and other plain-weave fabrics. The fabric is soaked in a sizing agent such as wheat-starch paste, glue, or pyroxylin, then dried. When rewetted or warmed, it can be shaped to create durable firm fabric for book covers, hats, and elements of clothing.

images.alt: Buckram is available in many colors.
